title: Deep Time: Dating Earth Then and Now
learningObjectives: Order key discoveries about geologic time from Steno to Patterson on a timeline.
Explain uniformitarianism as present processes shaping Earth in the past.
Describe how radioactive decay and half-life enable absolute dating of rocks.

evidence.quote: Radioactive decay solved the heat-flow question — with a source of heat in the cooling Earth, geologic time could be much longer
A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

explanations.text: Radioactive decay solved the cooling-Earth heat problem and half-life decay gave a clock for absolute rock ages.

evidence.quote: Nicholas Steno, 1669, gets credit for first writing down basic geological principles as laws.
The law of superposition says that older rocks are on the bottom and younger rocks are on the top.
In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.
Hutton said of geologic time that it had “no vestige of a beginning. No prospect of an end.”
The first geologic time scale was published in 1841 — Powell certainly would have known of it and used it in his geologic trips to the West.
